UDP (WireGuard and WARP, games, QUIC) carried in a TCP stream of the tunnel, sing-box\'s UDP-over-TCP v2. Only for a server that takes it: sing-box\'s naive inbound, a raycontrol node from v0.20.0 (its links turn it on with uot=2); elsewhere every UDP flow ends in EOF. Off, naive carries TCP only.

Use N concurrent tunnel connections to be more robust under bad network conditions. More connections make the tunneling easier to detect and less secure. This project strives for the strongest security against traffic analysis. Using it in an insecure way defeats its purpose. \n\nIf you must use this, try N=2 first to see if it solves your issues. Strongly recommend against using more than 4 connections here.

Where the profile carries UDP inside a TCP stream (VLESS/VMess/Trojan on any transport, REALITY among them, naive, DNS tunnels, Yggdrasil), QUIC is refused and browsers use TCP at once: QUIC inside TCP is slower than TCP itself. Profiles with UDP of their own (Hysteria2, WireGuard) keep it, and so does what goes direct. A routing rule of your own (protocol quic → block) refuses it everywhere instead.

An app\'s connection opens only once the node has reached the destination: a refused or unreachable one fails at once, with the reason in the log, instead of opening and ending empty. Each new connection waits one round trip to the node more. Only Hysteria2 of raycontrol nodes from v0.21.0 (their links say niko-ack=1).

On naive of raycontrol nodes that allow it (icmp=1), the node pings for the app: ping shows the real round trip and traceroute the hops behind the node. Off, a ping through a proxy is answered on the phone at once and says nothing about the path.

Hysteria2 and TUIC. A box that judges the flow by its first packets sees the fakes, or a ClientHello without the server name: a post-quantum ClientHello takes two Initial packets, and the second one goes first. A raycontrol node drops the fakes; for another server give them a TTL that ends before it (fewer hops than the server). Reordering does nothing under Hysteria2 obfs (no visible Initial there).

Before connecting, sends TCP SYNs or UDP datagrams to these ports of the server, in order. UDP steps may carry a hex payload: 1234/udp:68656c6c6f. SPA: 62201/spa:KEY sends one signed datagram that cannot be replayed (KEY = 64 hex digits, as on the server); 62201/spa1m:KEY hides its time too, if the server reads SPA v1m (v1 sends the time in clear, which DPI can match). Knocks again after a network change and when a connection fails. If a UDP session (WireGuard, Hysteria2, TUIC) gets no reply for the silence timeout after sending, knocks once more and logs whether the server answers again. Leave the sequence empty to disable.
Local proxy without password in VPN mode

Unsafe: any app on the device can use the local proxy and learn the server address. Needed for the system HTTP proxy option. In VPN mode the port opens only with this or with a local proxy password set.
